title: Cost: retention, throughput and the bill for a pipeline that never sleeps

videos.script: Three in the morning in Recife. Every shop is closed. Not one book has been sold since ten. {{night}} The cluster is still running. Three brokers, holding a week of sales on disk, three times over. {{cluster}} The consumers are running too, polling every second for sales that will not come until nine. {{idle}} A nightly job would cost twenty minutes tonight. A stream costs all twenty-four hours, every night. {{clock}} That is not a reason to avoid streaming. It is a reason to know the bill. {{bill}} In this lesson you measure what one sale costs on disk, with Kafka's own tools. {{measure}} You store the same hundred thousand sales four ways, and compare what compression saves. {{compress}} Then you turn the measurements into arithmetic. Sales a day, times bytes, times days kept, times copies. {{formula}} And you finish where the course began, with the question from lesson one. Does somebody act on the answer before the batch would have produced it? {{question}}
